title: Natural Selection and Adaptation Core Test
description: Core practice for inherited variation, environmental pressures, adaptation, and population change.

questions.prompt: What changes during natural selection?
questions.questionText: What changes during natural selection?
options: trait frequencies in a population over generations
one individual changing all its traits by choice
rocks choosing better shapes
an organism becoming perfect during one day
questions.correctAnswer: trait frequencies in a population over generations
questions.explanation: Natural selection explains population change over generations.

questions.prompt: Which condition must exist before natural selection can happen?
questions.questionText: Which condition must exist before natural selection can happen?
options: all individuals being identical
variation in inherited traits
no environmental differences
no traits affecting survival
questions.correctAnswer: variation in inherited traits
questions.explanation: Variation gives selection something to act on.

questions.prompt: A beetle population has green and brown beetles on dark bark. Birds more easily see green beetles. Which trait may become more common over generations?
questions.questionText: A beetle population has green and brown beetles on dark bark. Birds more easily see green beetles. Which trait may become more common over generations?
options: green coloration only
having no color
brown coloration
being seen more easily
questions.correctAnswer: brown coloration
questions.explanation: Brown beetles are harder to see in this environment, so that trait may become more common over generations.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows natural selection?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows natural selection?
options: need -> individual chooses trait -> instant perfection
sunlight -> no variation -> no population
fossil -> rock -> no evidence
variation -> environmental pressure -> survival differences -> trait pattern changes
questions.correctAnswer: variation -> environmental pressure -> survival differences -> trait pattern changes
questions.explanation: Natural selection depends on variation, environment, and population change over time.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Animals evolve because they try hard." What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Animals evolve because they try hard." What is the best correction?
options: Inherited variation already exists, and the environment affects which traits are helpful.
Trying hard creates new inherited traits instantly.
Environment never matters.
Populations do not change.
questions.correctAnswer: Inherited variation already exists, and the environment affects which traits are helpful.
questions.explanation: Natural selection is not about effort or choice; it is about inherited variation and environmental effects.

questions.prompt: In a dry year, finches with deeper beaks crack tough seeds better. Which claim is best supported if deeper-beaked finches become more common later?
questions.questionText: In a dry year, finches with deeper beaks crack tough seeds better. Which claim is best supported if deeper-beaked finches become more common later?
options: Finches chose deeper beaks because they wanted them.
The dry environment favored a beak trait that helped with available food.
Tough seeds made every individual change beaks immediately.
Beak traits cannot affect feeding.
questions.correctAnswer: The dry environment favored a beak trait that helped with available food.
questions.explanation: The trait helped in that environment and became more common over generations.

questions.prompt: Which example is an adaptation?
questions.questionText: Which example is an adaptation?
options: any feature an organism wishes for
a temporary injury
a heritable trait that helps organisms survive in a particular environment
a label written by a scientist
questions.correctAnswer: a heritable trait that helps organisms survive in a particular environment
questions.explanation: An adaptation is a heritable trait that improves success in a specific environment.

questions.prompt: A light-colored mouse is easier for owls to see on dark lava rock. Which cause/effect chain is strongest?
questions.questionText: A light-colored mouse is easier for owls to see on dark lava rock. Which cause/effect chain is strongest?
options: visible fur -> mouse chooses dark fur immediately
dark rock -> owls stop hunting
light fur -> no effect on survival
visible fur -> more likely eaten -> fewer light-fur traits in future generations
questions.correctAnswer: visible fur -> more likely eaten -> fewer light-fur traits in future generations
questions.explanation: Visibility can affect predation and change trait frequencies over generations.

questions.prompt: Which data would best support natural selection in a bacteria population?
questions.questionText: Which data would best support natural selection in a bacteria population?
options: After antibiotic exposure, the resistant-trait frequency increases.
The petri dish is round.
The bacteria have names.
The lab has bright lights.
questions.correctAnswer: After antibiotic exposure, the resistant-trait frequency increases.
questions.explanation: A trait becoming more common after an environmental pressure supports natural selection.

questions.prompt: Why does natural selection not make organisms perfect?
questions.questionText: Why does natural selection not make organisms perfect?
options: Every helpful trait is perfect everywhere.
Traits are helpful only in certain environments and involve tradeoffs.
All organisms choose the best trait.
Variation disappears before environments change.
questions.correctAnswer: Traits are helpful only in certain environments and involve tradeoffs.
questions.explanation: Adaptations are context-dependent and may have tradeoffs.

questions.prompt: A white fur trait helps in snowy habitats but stands out in dark forest soil. What does this show?
questions.questionText: A white fur trait helps in snowy habitats but stands out in dark forest soil. What does this show?
options: White fur is always best.
Dark soil has no effect on visibility.
Whether a trait helps can depend on the environment.
Traits are never connected to survival.
questions.correctAnswer: Whether a trait helps can depend on the environment.
questions.explanation: A trait can be helpful in one environment and less helpful in another.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares individuals and populations?
questions.questionText: Which statement correctly compares individuals and populations?
options: Individuals evolve completely during one lifetime.
Populations have no variation.
Traits are never measured in groups.
Individuals have traits; populations can change in trait frequency over generations.
questions.correctAnswer: Individuals have traits; populations can change in trait frequency over generations.
questions.explanation: Evolution is described as population change over generations.

questions.prompt: A graph shows pesticide resistance rising from 5% to 60% over many insect generations. Which explanation fits?
questions.questionText: A graph shows pesticide resistance rising from 5% to 60% over many insect generations. Which explanation fits?
options: Resistant insects survived the pesticide better, so the trait became more common.
Each insect decided to become resistant.
Pesticide made all insects identical instantly.
Resistance cannot be inherited.
questions.correctAnswer: Resistant insects survived the pesticide better, so the trait became more common.
questions.explanation: The population pattern supports selection for a resistant trait.

questions.prompt: Which investigation would best test whether camouflage affects survival?
questions.questionText: Which investigation would best test whether camouflage affects survival?
options: Ask which model looks nicest.
Compare how often predators find models of different colors in the same habitat.
Use one model once without counting results.
Change color, size, shape, and location all at once.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare how often predators find models of different colors in the same habitat.
questions.explanation: A fair test compares color visibility while controlling other factors.

questions.prompt: A drought changes available seeds from small soft seeds to large tough seeds. What trait might be favored?
questions.questionText: A drought changes available seeds from small soft seeds to large tough seeds. What trait might be favored?
options: weaker beaks that cannot crack seeds
brighter feathers unrelated to feeding
beaks better at cracking tough seeds
shorter legs because seeds are tough
questions.correctAnswer: beaks better at cracking tough seeds
questions.explanation: A feeding trait that helps with the available food may be favored.

questions.prompt: A student claims, "Every trait that is common must be helpful." Which response is best?
questions.questionText: A student claims, "Every trait that is common must be helpful." Which response is best?
options: Common always means best.
Rare traits are always harmful.
Data are not needed.
A trait can be common for several reasons; evidence is needed to show it helps.
questions.correctAnswer: A trait can be common for several reasons; evidence is needed to show it helps.
questions.explanation: Trait frequency alone does not prove a trait is adaptive.

questions.prompt: Which model revision improves this chain: environment -> adaptation?
questions.questionText: Which model revision improves this chain: environment -> adaptation?
options: environment -> survival differences among existing variations -> helpful trait becomes more common
environment -> organisms choose new traits
environment -> no variation -> adaptation
environment -> every individual becomes perfect
questions.correctAnswer: environment -> survival differences among existing variations -> helpful trait becomes more common
questions.explanation: The improved model shows existing variation and population-level change.

questions.prompt: A fish population includes fast and slow swimmers. A new predator catches slower fish more often. Which claim is most reasonable?
questions.questionText: A fish population includes fast and slow swimmers. A new predator catches slower fish more often. Which claim is most reasonable?
options: Slow fish will choose fast traits instantly.
Fast-swimming traits may become more common if they are inherited.
Predators cannot affect populations.
Swimming speed can never matter.
questions.correctAnswer: Fast-swimming traits may become more common if they are inherited.
questions.explanation: If a heritable trait affects survival, its frequency may change over generations.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would weaken a natural-selection explanation for shell color?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would weaken a natural-selection explanation for shell color?
options: Shell colors vary.
Predators eat some snails.
Shell color does not affect survival, and color frequency stays the same across generations.
Habitats have backgrounds.
questions.correctAnswer: Shell color does not affect survival, and color frequency stays the same across generations.
questions.explanation: No survival difference and no frequency change would weaken the explanation.

questions.prompt: Why is inherited variation important in antibiotic resistance?
questions.questionText: Why is inherited variation important in antibiotic resistance?
options: Every cell learns resistance by trying.
Antibiotics are food for all bacteria.
Resistance is unrelated to survival.
Resistant cells already present can survive and become a larger share of the population.
questions.correctAnswer: Resistant cells already present can survive and become a larger share of the population.
questions.explanation: Selection can increase the frequency of existing resistant variants.

questions.prompt: Which statement best handles tradeoffs?
questions.questionText: Which statement best handles tradeoffs?
options: A trait that helps avoid predators might also require more energy or reduce success elsewhere.
Helpful traits never have costs.
Tradeoffs make evidence unnecessary.
Only harmful traits have effects.
questions.correctAnswer: A trait that helps avoid predators might also require more energy or reduce success elsewhere.
questions.explanation: Adaptations can involve benefits and costs depending on context.

questions.prompt: A graph shows dark moths increase after tree bark darkens from pollution. Later, light bark returns and light moths increase. What does this show?
questions.questionText: A graph shows dark moths increase after tree bark darkens from pollution. Later, light bark returns and light moths increase. What does this show?
options: Moths choose color each morning.
Changing environments can change which trait is favored.
Only one trait can ever exist.
Natural selection has no connection to environment.
questions.correctAnswer: Changing environments can change which trait is favored.
questions.explanation: The favored trait depends on environmental conditions.

questions.prompt: Which question would best test if a trait is heritable in a selection explanation?
questions.questionText: Which question would best test if a trait is heritable in a selection explanation?
options: Is the trait easy to draw?
Does the trait have a long name?
Do related individuals tend to show similar forms of the trait?
Can the organism be seen from far away?
questions.correctAnswer: Do related individuals tend to show similar forms of the trait?
questions.explanation: Natural selection requires traits that can be passed across generations.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Natural selection always helps every individual." Which correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Natural selection always helps every individual." Which correction is best?
options: Every individual always benefits equally.
Populations never change.
Traits cannot affect survival.
Selection describes population patterns; some individuals survive less successfully.
questions.correctAnswer: Selection describes population patterns; some individuals survive less successfully.
questions.explanation: Selection can favor some traits while individuals with other traits are less successful.

questions.prompt: Which scenario best shows natural selection rather than learning?
questions.questionText: Which scenario best shows natural selection rather than learning?
options: A shell-color trait becomes more common across many generations because predators spot one color more easily.
A dog learns a command.
A student memorizes a route home.
A plant bends toward light during one week.
questions.correctAnswer: A shell-color trait becomes more common across many generations because predators spot one color more easily.
questions.explanation: Natural selection involves inherited trait frequencies changing over generations.

questions.prompt: A drought lasts five years. Birds with beaks matching the remaining seeds have higher survival. Which data would strengthen the explanation?
questions.questionText: A drought lasts five years. Birds with beaks matching the remaining seeds have higher survival. Which data would strengthen the explanation?
options: one drawing of a bird
beak measurements and survival rates across several generations
a list of bird names only
the color of the measuring tape
questions.correctAnswer: beak measurements and survival rates across several generations
questions.explanation: Trait and survival data across generations directly support selection.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best connects natural selection to biodiversity?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best connects natural selection to biodiversity?
options: Natural selection removes all variety instantly.
Biodiversity means all organisms are identical.
Different environments can favor different traits, contributing to variety among populations.
Environments cannot affect trait patterns.
questions.correctAnswer: Different environments can favor different traits, contributing to variety among populations.
questions.explanation: Selection in different environments can help explain differences among populations.

questions.prompt: A model includes variation, environment, survival, and trait-frequency change. What key natural-selection idea is still missing?
questions.questionText: A model includes variation, environment, survival, and trait-frequency change. What key natural-selection idea is still missing?
options: the organism must choose the trait
the model must ignore evidence
the environment must stay exactly the same forever
the trait must be inherited to change future population patterns
questions.correctAnswer: the trait must be inherited to change future population patterns
questions.explanation: Selection affects future populations when helpful traits are inherited.

questions.prompt: Which claim is most scientifically careful?
questions.questionText: Which claim is most scientifically careful?
options: The data suggest the darker color trait was favored in the dark-bark environment.
Dark color is always best in every habitat.
All individuals changed color because they needed to.
One photo proves every generation.
questions.correctAnswer: The data suggest the darker color trait was favored in the dark-bark environment.
questions.explanation: The careful claim stays tied to the specific evidence and environment.

questions.prompt: Which final summary best shows natural-selection understanding?
questions.questionText: Which final summary best shows natural-selection understanding?
options: Individuals evolve by wanting new traits.
Existing inherited variation interacts with environmental pressures, causing helpful traits to become more or less common over generations.
Traits are never connected to survival.
Populations cannot change over time.
questions.correctAnswer: Existing inherited variation interacts with environmental pressures, causing helpful traits to become more or less common over generations.
questions.explanation: This summary includes variation, environment, inheritance, and population change over generations.
